"""Pagination helper shared by the listing tools."""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.pagination import ItemT, PaginatedResult


async def iter_pages(
    fetch: Callable[[int], Awaitable[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]],
    *,
    page: int | None,
    per_page: int,
) -> AsyncIterator[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]:
    """Yield the pages of a paginated Tracker listing.

    ``page`` returns that single page; None walks the listing from the first
    one. A page shorter than ``per_page`` is the last one, so a full walk does
    not spend a request on the empty page past the end of the data.
    """
    current_page = 1 if page is None else page

    while True:
        batch = await fetch(current_page)
        if not batch.values:
            return

        yield batch

        if page is not None or len(batch.values) < per_page:
            return

        current_page += 1


def restricted_totals_unavailable(restricted: bool, page: int | None) -> bool:
    """Return True when a listing's reported totals would misdescribe the result.

    The `X-Total-Count` / `X-Total-Pages` headers count what Tracker matched,
    before this server drops the queues the caller may not see, so they are only
    reported when no allow-list is configured. They are also pointless on a full
    walk, which already returned every item there is.
    """
    return restricted or page is None
=== utils ===
def set_non_needed_fields_null(data: Iterable[T], needed_fields: set[str]) -> None:
    for item in data:
        model_fields = type(item).model_fields
        extra = item.__pydantic_extra__
        # `model_fields_set` is mutated below, so iterate over a snapshot.
        for field in tuple(item.model_fields_set):
            if field in needed_fields:
                continue

            if extra is not None and field in extra:
                # Fields the API returned that the model does not declare
                # (`self`, `id`, `queue`, `boards`, the queue's own
                # `<queue-id>--<key>` fields) live in `__pydantic_extra__`,
                # which carries no `exclude_if=none_excluder`. Nulling one
                # leaves it in the response as an explicit `null`, so dropping
                # it is the only way to honour the field selection.
                del extra[field]
                item.__pydantic_fields_set__.discard(field)
                continue

            field_info = model_fields.get(field)
            # Skip fields whose declared type doesn't allow None (e.g. required
            # `id: int`) - nulling them would produce a response that violates
            # the tool's own output schema.
            if field_info is not None and type(None) not in get_args(
                field_info.annotation
            ):
                continue
            setattr(item, field, None)

The "collect pages, then decide whether the totals survive" block is written twice, near-identically.

Both sites carry a `last_page: PaginatedResult[X] | None = None` accumulator reassigned every iteration, a `hide_totals = restricted_totals_unavailable(bool(settings.tracker_limit_queues), page)` call, and the same ternary pair `hits=None if hide_totals or last_page is None else last_page.hits` / `pages=…` — four ternaries, two accumulators, two `bool()` wrappers. `restricted_totals_unavailable` is itself a one-line `restricted or page is None` that gets a dedicated 4-case parametrized test class (`TestRestrictedTotalsUnavailable` in tests/mcp/tools/test_pagination.py) — a test for `a or b`.

Simpler form — one collector next to `iter_pages` that absorbs the predicate:

```python
async def collect_pages(
    fetch: Callable[[int], Awaitable[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]],
    *,
    page: int | None,
    per_page: int,
    totals_trustworthy: bool = True,
) -> PaginatedResult[ItemT]:
    values: list[ItemT] = []
    last: PaginatedResult[ItemT] | None = None
    async for batch in iter_pages(fetch, page=page, per_page=per_page):
        values.extend(batch.values)
        last = batch
    # Totals count what Tracker matched, before this server hides queues, and a
    # full walk already returned everything there is.
    if page is None or last is None or not totals_trustworthy:
        return PaginatedResult[ItemT](values=values)
    return PaginatedResult[ItemT](values=values, hits=last.hits, pages=last.pages)
```

`queues_get_all` becomes that one call plus its allow-list filter over `result.values`; `_collect_templates` becomes the same call plus `_visible_templates`. Filtering after the walk instead of per batch is equivalent — `iter_pages` decides exhaustion from the unfiltered `batch.values`. `restricted_totals_unavailable` and its test class then go away.

That discard is the sole mutation of `model_fields_set` inside the loop, so the `tuple(...)` copy on line 50 and the comment on line 49 exist only to support a line that does nothing.

Simpler form: delete line 62, restore `for field in item.model_fields_set:` on line 50, drop the comment on line 49. I ran tests/mcp/tools/test_issue_read_tools.py, test_user_tools.py and test_queue_tools.py (58 tests) against exactly that version — all pass.

**`mcp_tracker/mcp/tools/_pagination.py:22-32` — the pagination walk stays strictly sequential even though this diff now hands it `X-Total-Pages` on the first response.**

ALTITUDE REVIEW — 5 findings (one verified by running the code).

**1. `mcp_tracker/tracker/proto/types/pagination.py:10` — the new generic envelope doesn't absorb the three hand-rolled ones that already existed.**
`ProjectSearchResult` / `PortfolioSearchResult` / `GoalSearchResult` (`mcp_tracker/tracker/proto/types/entities.py:306-321`) are already exactly `{hits, pages, values}`, returned by `project_find`/`portfolio_find`/`goal_find`. `PaginatedResult` was added beside them, so one concept now has two envelopes that don't behave the same: the old trio uses `NoneExcludedField` so the totals *vanish* when null, the new one emits them as explicit `null` and documents what null means — and only the new one carries field descriptions. Cost: every future change to the pagination contract has to be made twice and kept identical by hand, and the client-facing shape is already inconsistent across tools. Deeper fix: `ProjectSearchResult = PaginatedResult[ProjectEntity]` (alias or subclass) and delete the trio.
Corollary at the docs layer: `mcp_tracker/mcp/tools/project.py:58`, `portfolio.py:58`, `goal.py:57` still say "call again with `page` incremented … until an empty result is returned" while the five converted tools had that sentence removed, and `mcp_tracker/mcp/params.py:609` (the server-wide instructions — the layer that owns "how pagination works here") still teaches only page-until-exhausted, with no mention of `hits`/`pages`. """Pagination helpers shared by the listing tools."""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.pagination import ItemT, PaginatedResult


async def iter_pages(
    fetch: Callable[[int], Awaitable[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]],
    *,
    page: int | None,
    per_page: int,
) -> AsyncIterator[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]:
    """Yield the pages of a paginated Tracker listing.

    ``page`` returns that single page; None walks the listing from the first
    one. A walk stops as soon as the data is exhausted, which is either the
    page count Tracker reports or - when it reports none - a page shorter than
    ``per_page``.
    """
    current_page = 1 if page is None else page

    while True:
        batch = await fetch(current_page)
        if not batch.values:
            return

        yield batch

        if page is not None:
            return
        if batch.pages is not None:
            # Tracker says how many pages there are, so the walk can stop on the
            # last one instead of spending a request on the empty page past it.
            if current_page >= batch.pages:
                return
        elif len(batch.values) < per_page:
            return

        current_page += 1


async def collect_pages(
    fetch: Callable[[int], Awaitable[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]],
    *,
    page: int | None,
    per_page: int,
    visible: Callable[[list[ItemT]], list[ItemT]] | None = None,
    restricted: bool = False,
) -> PaginatedResult[ItemT]:
    """Collect ``page`` alone, or every page, into one result.

    ``visible`` filters each batch down to what the caller may see. Doing so
    makes the totals Tracker reported describe more than ``values`` holds, so
    they are dropped whenever ``restricted`` says a filter is configured - as
    they are on a full walk, which already returned every item there is.
    Keeping that decision here is what stops a new listing tool from reporting
    totals that count the rows it just hid.
    """
    values: list[ItemT] = []
    last_page: PaginatedResult[ItemT] | None = None

    async for batch in iter_pages(fetch, page=page, per_page=per_page):
        last_page = batch
        values.extend(visible(batch.values) if visible else batch.values)

    if last_page is None or restricted or page is None:
        return PaginatedResult[ItemT](values=values)

    return PaginatedResult[ItemT](
        values=values, hits=last_page.hits, pages=last_page.pages
    )

Готово. `task` зелёный, 1222 теста.

Про пустую константу — вы поймали ровно то, что должен был поймать я: я оставил `= ""`, чтобы не трогать 39 мест. Удалил и её, и 45 конкатенаций `+ ENTITY_QUEUE_RESTRICTIONS_NOTE` в 6 модулях.

## Применено

**Общий коллектор страниц** (нашли 3 агента из 4). Блок «обойти → запомнить последнюю страницу → решить про totals → собрать конверт» был написан дважды. Теперь `collect_pages()` в `_pagination.py` владеет этим решением, а `restricted_totals_unavailable` удалён — правило «totals не переживают отфильтрованный обход» больше не соглашение, о котором новый тул может забыть.

**`iter_pages` перестал зондировать конец** (efficiency + altitude). Он получал `pages` и выбрасывал: листинг, размер которого кратен `per_page`, всегда тратил лишний запрос на пустую страницу. Теперь останавливается по счётчику, с откатом на старое поведение, если заголовка нет. Проверил на живом API: 393 очереди за 4 запроса.

**Один конверт вместо двух** (reuse + altitude). `ProjectSearchResult` / `PortfolioSearchResult` / `GoalSearchResult` были поле в поле теми же `{values, hits, pages}` — стали алиасами `PaginatedResult[...]`. Побочно entity-тулы получили описание контракта null, которого у них не было.

Плюс: убрал из описаний трёх entity-тулов устаревшее «листайте до пустого ответа» (контракт теперь один раз в `instructions`), упростил тройной тернарник в `issues_find`, перевёл 11 ручных конструкций в тестах на общий `page()`, откатил `RequestCapture(headers=...)` — у `aioresponses` есть родной `headers=`.

## Отклонено

**«`discard` из `__pydantic_fields_set__` — no-op»** — не подтвердилось. Он действительно не влияет на сериализацию, но держит функцию идемпотентной:

```
без discard, 2-й проход: {'key': 'K-1', 'self': None, 'id': None}
```

То есть возвращаются ровно те `null`, ради устранения которых правка делалась. При 15 вызовах в 8 модулях оставил, комментарий теперь объясняет причину.

Также отклонил: параллельную загрузку страниц (реальный выигрыш по латентности, но это смена паттерна запросов к rate-limited API — не уборка), обобщение `resolve_issue_field` до `make_field_resolver(model)` (нужен ровно одной модели), перенос `IssuesCount` в слой `mcp/` (косметика).

## Нашлось попутно — это баг, и я его не чинил

Агент по altitude проверил остальные вызовы `set_non_needed_fields_null`, я перепроверил сам:


content.text:
Починил. `task` зелёный, 1240 тестов.

## Что было

Дефект оказался с двумя причинами, а не с одной. Первую (extras с `null`) я закрыл раньше — она объясняла мусор в `issues_find`. Вторая жила рядом и её не было видно на `Issue`: четыре модели объявляли опциональные поля голым `Field(None)`, без `exclude_if`, поэтому занулённое поле оставалось в ответе.

Перепись показала ровно, где течёт:

```
OK   Issue            0/25      LEAK User             6/8
OK   Queue            0/7       LEAK IssueComment     4/11
OK   ProjectFields    0/19      LEAK Worklog          4/9
OK   PortfolioFields  0/18      LEAK IssueAttachment  4/8
OK   GoalFields       0/17
```

18 полей в 4 моделях. `Issue` и `Queue` были в порядке, потому что им `NoneExcludedField` проставили при прошлых правках; entity-модели — потому что их писали позже и уже с ним.

## После

```
users_get_all(fields=['login'])  -> {'uid': 1, 'login': 'bob'}
comments(fields=['text'])        -> {'id': 1, 'text': 'hi'}
worklogs(fields=['duration'])    -> {'id': 1, 'duration': 1:00:00}
attachments(fields=['name'])     -> {'id': '1', 'name': 'f.png'}
```

Остаются только обязательные поля (`uid`, `id`, `name`) — их занулить нельзя, это сломало бы output schema тула, — плюс запрошенное.

## Инвариант

`tests/mcp/tools/test_field_selection.py` держит правило для всех девяти моделей, до которых дотягивается селектор. Два теста на модель: что у каждого nullable-поля есть `exclude_if`, и сквозной — что после фильтрации в ответе не остаётся ничего лишнего.

Проверил, что он ловит регрессию: вернул одно поле к `Field(None)` → два падения с сообщением, что нужно поставить `NoneExcludedField`.

`Issue` включён в список, хотя своего enum у него больше нет — `issues_find` принимает свободные строки, но фильтруется тем же хелпером, так что правило то же.

Обновил CHANGELOG. README трогать не стал: там описание `fields` и так обещает фильтрацию — теперь оно просто соответствует поведению.

cat > $SP/stage.py <<'PY'
"""Stage selected hunks of a file's diff into the index.

`git add -p` is interactive and unavailable here, so hunks are picked by regex
against their own text and replayed with `git apply --cached --unidiff-zero`.
"""
import re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, os

def hunks(path):
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "-U0", "--", path],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    if not out.strip():
        return "", []
    head, *rest = re.split(r"(?m)^(?=@@ )", out)
    return head, rest

def stage(path, include=None, exclude=None):
    head, hs = hunks(path)
    if not hs:
        print(f"  {path}: no diff"); return 0
    picked = []
    for h in hs:
        body = "".join(l for l in h.splitlines(True) if l[:1] in "+-" and l[:3] not in ("+++", "---"))
        if include and not re.search(include, body):
            continue
        if exclude and re.search(exclude, body):
            continue
        picked.append(h)
    if not picked:
        print(f"  {path}: 0/{len(hs)} hunks"); return 0
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".patch", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(head + "".join(picked)); patch = f.name
    subprocess.run(["git", "apply", "--cached", "--unidiff-zero", patch], check=True)
    os.unlink(patch)
    print(f"  {path}: {len(picked)}/{len(hs)} hunks staged")
    return len(picked)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    path = sys.argv[1]
    inc = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 and sys.argv[2] else None
    exc = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 and sys.argv[3] else None
    stage(path, inc, exc)
PY

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix: honour the `fields` selector instead of blanking fields

Asking a tool for a subset of fields returned the whole object with the
unwanted fields set to `null` rather than dropped, so the parameter that
exists to save context window did nothing. Two causes:

- Fields the API returns that the model does not declare (`self`, `id`,
  `statusStartTime`, `queue`, `boards`, `favorite`, a queue's own
  `<queue-id>--<key>` local fields) live in `__pydantic_extra__`, which
  carries no `exclude_if`. Nulling one left it in the payload as an
  explicit `null`, so they are now deleted outright. Discarding the name
  from `__pydantic_fields_set__` too keeps a second pass idempotent -
  without it the extra is re-added as `None`.
- `User`, `IssueComment`, `Worklog` and `IssueAttachment` declared their
  optional fields with a bare `Field(None)`, so a blanked field stayed in
  the payload for the same reason. `Issue` and `Queue` already used
  `NoneExcludedField`.

`tests/mcp/tools/test_field_selection.py` now fails if a model reachable
from a `fields` selector forgets `exclude_if`.

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat: report pagination totals from the paginated listings

Every `page`/`perPage` endpoint answers with `X-Total-Count` and
`X-Total-Pages`, and the client dropped both. A caller could only learn
whether a page was the last one by requesting the next one and getting an
empty list, and `issues_find` in particular gave no way to size a result
set at all.

The five listings - `issues_find`, `users_get_all`, `queues_get_all`,
`issue_templates_get_all`, `comment_templates_get_all` - now answer with
the shared `PaginatedResult` envelope `{values, hits, pages}` instead of
a bare list. The entity search results, which already had exactly that
shape parsed out of the response body, become aliases of it, so one
concept has one type and one documented contract.

`collect_pages` owns the walk and the decision to withhold the totals:
they count what Tracker matched, before this server hides queues the
caller may not see, so they are reported only for an explicit single page
on an unrestricted server. Keeping that in the helper is what stops a new
listing tool from reporting totals for rows it just filtered out.

`iter_pages` also stops on the page count Tracker reports rather than
probing, which saves a request whenever a listing's size is an exact
multiple of `per_page`.

BREAKING: consumers that iterated the top-level result of those five
tools must now iterate `values`.

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat: select issue fields through the API, and accept any field name

`issues_find` fetched every field and then blanked the unwanted ones
locally. The search endpoint takes a `fields` query parameter and
projects server-side, so the selection now travels with the request and
unwanted fields are never fetched: asking for `["key"]` returns five keys
per issue instead of thirty.

The selector also stops being a closed enum built from `Issue`'s declared
fields, which left 12 of the 37 fields Tracker returns unreachable -
`resolution`, `queue`, `project`, `followers` and the rest, plus every
queue-local and organization-custom field. It now takes any name, and
`resolve_issue_field` maps the three spellings that reach it: a declared
field named the Python way (`story_points`), the same field named
Tracker's way (`storyPoints`), and a name this server does not declare,
which passes through and arrives in the model's extras.

Verified against the live API: local fields resolve by their `id`
(`<queue-id>--<key>`), not their short `key`, and an unknown name is
answered 200 with the field simply absent - so the parameter's
description points at `queue_get_fields` and says a missing field means
the name was wrong.

content.content:
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## [0.8.0-dev] - unreleased

### Features
- Add `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES` for per-queue read-only access ([closes #36](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/issues/36))
  - One instance can now be read-write on some queues and read-only on others, instead of running two
  - Write tools stay registered; each mutating call validates its target queue against the allow-list, while reads are unaffected
- Add read-only issue and comment template tools ([fixes #43](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/issues/43), [#48](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/pull/48))
  - `issue_templates_get_all` / `issue_template_get` return the templates teams keep for bugs, incidents and other recurring work, including the `fieldTemplates` values they prefill
  - `comment_templates_get_all` / `comment_template_get` return the wording teams reuse when replying, with the users and mailing lists such a comment summons
  - Both listings take an optional `queue` and answer with that queue's templates plus the ones bound to no queue, which are usable everywhere
  - Both walk every page by default (the endpoints paginate at 50 items, so a single request used to be a silent truncation) and accept `page` / `per_page` for one page at a time
  - `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` is enforced: templates of a restricted queue are dropped from the listings and rejected on direct access, and a restricted `queue` argument is refused before the request
  - Neither endpoint is in the public API reference; the models follow the official `yandex_tracker_client` collections and keep undeclared response fields instead of dropping them
- Give `issue_create` the typed reference parameters `issue_update` already had - `parent`, `sprint`, `followers`, `components`, `tags`, `project`, `markup_type` - so a value that works in one tool works in the other
- Add `assignee` and `components` to `issue_update`
- `fields` maps on `issue_create` / `issue_update` now override the dedicated parameter of the same name, which is how a field is cleared: `{"assignee": null}` clears it, where an unset parameter is simply not sent
- `queue_get_metadata` actually returns what `expand` asked for, and answers a requested but empty section with an empty list instead of leaving it out
- `get_priorities` returns the priority `id` and `description`
- Add MCP tools for Yandex Tracker projects, portfolios and goals — the entities API, distinct from queues and issues
  - Read: `project_get`/`project_find`, `portfolio_get`/`portfolio_find`, `goal_get`/`goal_find`, each with an explicit per-entity `fields` selector defaulting to a small base field set
  - Write: create/update/delete per entity type, with optimistic concurrency via `version`
  - Comments: add/update/delete plus cursor-paginated `*_get_comments`
  - Checklists (projects and portfolios only — the API does not define them for goals): add, edit, move, delete a single item, bulk-edit all items, delete the whole checklist

- `issues_find` accepts any field name in `fields`, not only the ones `Issue` declares: standard fields the model omits (`resolution`, `queue`, `project`, `followers`, ...), a queue's local fields and an organization's custom ones are selectable at all for the first time - pass the field `id` from `queue_get_fields`
  - Both spellings of a declared field work (`story_points` and `storyPoints`); Tracker silently ignores a name it does not know, which the parameter's description says
- Add `TRACKER_API_TIMEOUT` (default `10`) - the per-request Tracker API timeout was hardcoded and could not be raised for slow queries

  - Keeping them off by default also keeps the tool manifest at its previous size (39 tools); enabling adds 39 more

- Entity responses now use Tracker's own field names instead of the Python ones: `storyPoints`, `createdAt`, `updatedBy`, `textHtml`, `executedTriggers`, `maillistSummonees` and the rest, matching what the same fields are called on input. - Change `issues_count` from a bare integer to `{"count": N}`
- Change the `issue_get_comments` result from `list[IssueComment]` to the cursor-paginated `{comments, next_cursor}` object

- `issue_create` no longer answers 422 for `components: ["694"]` or `followers: ["8000000000000034"]`: reference values are typed models shared with `issue_update` and serialized identically, with `IssueComponentRef` requiring exactly one of `id` / `name` because Tracker reads a bare string there as a component *name*

- `assignee` and `parent` can be cleared at all (previously `null` was unreachable and `""` answered 422)
- An empty reference object (`type={}`) is refused locally with a readable message instead of an unhelpful 400/422 from Tracker
- API errors carry Tracker's own `errorMessages` / `errors` in `TrackerAPIError` instead of a bare "Unprocessable Entity"
- 409 on update raises `IssueVersionConflict`, which explains that queue triggers bump the version right after creation, so the version returned by `issue_create` must not be reused
- A missing queue raises `QueueNotFound` on every queue-scoped read (`queue_get`, `queues_get_tags`, `queues_get_versions`, `queues_get_local_fields`, `queues_get_fields`), not just on the newest ones
- `queue_get_fields` is described as what it is - the fields configured on the queue - and points at `get_global_fields` for the rest; system fields such as `parent` or `estimation` are settable without appearing in the queue listing
- `get_priorities` is findable by tool search: its description now names the priority levels and the parameter it feeds
- Issue templates expose a single, normalized `description`; the issue body a template prefills stays in `fieldTemplates.description`
- Reject an entity update that would only change `links` instead of reporting a no-op as success
  - Yandex Tracker answers 200 but ignores `links` unless the same request also changes a field or carries a `comment`; the entity's `version` does not even advance
  - `links` are added rather than replaced: re-sending an existing link fails, links cannot be read back or removed through the server, and each relationship is only valid against a particular target entity type. All of this is now stated in the tool descriptions

- Fall back to the per-entity default field set when `fields` is an empty list, which previously sent `fields=` and returned an entity with no fields populated
- Describe `*_update_checklist` as the bulk edit of existing items that it is: a partial list, or one that changes the item count, is rejected by the API with a 500
- Drop `with_board` from `goal_delete`: goals have no board

### Internal
- `lastCommentUpdatedAt` is typed as `datetime` rather than `date | datetime`, which made the serialized type depend on whether the timestamp landed exactly on midnight

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("CHANGELOG.md")
s = p.read_text()
start = s.index("## [0.8.0-dev] - unreleased")
end = s.index("## [0.7.3] - 2026-07-28")

new = '''## [0.8.0-dev] - unreleased

### Features

- **Project, portfolio and goal tools** — the entities API, distinct from queues and issues ([#45](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/pull/45))
  - 43 tools: get/find, create/update/delete, comments, and checklists (projects and portfolios only — the API has none for goals)
  - Off by default behind `TRACKER_ENTITIES_ENABLED`: they double the tool manifest and are not covered by `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` / `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`, since an entity has no single queue. `TRACKER_READ_ONLY` still unregisters the write tools
  - `links` are added, never replaced, and are write-only in Tracker: an existing link cannot be re-sent, read back, or removed through this server. A links-only update is rejected rather than reported as a success Tracker silently ignores
  - `*_update_checklist` is a bulk edit of all existing items; a partial list is rejected by the API with a 500
- **Issue and comment template tools**, read-only ([#43](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/issues/43), [#48](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/pull/48))
  - `issue_templates_get_all` / `issue_template_get`, `comment_templates_get_all` / `comment_template_get`
  - The issue body a template prefills is in `fieldTemplates.description`, not the template's own `description`
  - Optional `queue` scoping, every page retrieved by default, `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` enforced
- **`TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`** — per-queue read-only access, so one instance can be read-write on some queues and read-only on others ([#36](https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/issues/36))
- **`TRACKER_API_TIMEOUT`** (default `10`) — the per-request Tracker timeout was hardcoded and could not be raised
- **Paginated listings report their totals.** `issues_find`, `users_get_all`, `queues_get_all` and both template listings answer with `{values, hits, pages}`, built from the `X-Total-Count` / `X-Total-Pages` headers the client used to discard. The last page no longer has to be found by requesting the empty one after it
  - Totals are withheld where they would mislead: on a full walk, and when `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` hides rows Tracker counted
- **`issues_find` selects fields through the API** (`_search?fields=`), so unwanted fields are never fetched instead of fetched and dropped
  - `fields` now takes any field name, not just the 25 `Issue` declares: `resolution`, `queue`, `project`, `followers`, queue-local and organization-custom fields become selectable. Pass the field `id` from `queue_get_fields`; both `story_points` and `storyPoints` work
- `issue_create` gained the typed reference parameters `issue_update` already had (`parent`, `sprint`, `followers`, `components`, `tags`, `project`, `markup_type`), and `issue_update` gained `assignee` and `components`
- A `fields` map on `issue_create` / `issue_update` overrides the dedicated parameter of the same name, which is how a field is cleared: `{"assignee": null}` clears it
- `get_priorities` returns each priority's `id` and `description`

### Breaking Changes

- Responses use Tracker's own field names instead of the Python ones: `storyPoints`, `createdAt`, `updatedBy`, `textHtml` and the rest. A response can now be fed straight back into a `fields` map; callers reading `story_points` or `created_at` need updating
- `issues_find`, `users_get_all`, `queues_get_all`, `issue_templates_get_all` and `comment_templates_get_all` return `{values, hits, pages}` instead of a bare list — iterate `values`
- `issues_count` returns `{"count": N}` instead of a bare integer, which for a project of 403 issues was indistinguishable from an HTTP 403
- `issue_get_comments` returns the cursor-paginated `{comments, next_cursor}` instead of a list, and without pagination arguments returns the first 50 comments rather than all of them

### Bug Fixes

- `fields` actually filters the response instead of blanking it, in every tool that offers the selector. Asking `issues_find` for `["key"]` used to return a dozen null keys per issue
  - Undeclared fields the API returns (`self`, `id`, `queue`, a queue's `<queue-id>--<key>` local fields) sat in the model's extras, which carry no `exclude_if`, so blanking left them as explicit nulls; they are now dropped
  - `User`, `IssueComment`, `Worklog` and `IssueAttachment` declared optionals with a bare `Field(None)` and leaked nulls the same way. A test now fails if a model reachable from a `fields` selector forgets `exclude_if`
- `issue_create` no longer answers 422 for `components: ["694"]` or `followers: ["8000000000000034"]`: reference values are typed models shared with `issue_update`, with `IssueComponentRef` requiring exactly one of `id` / `name` because Tracker reads a bare string there as a component *name*
- A key in `fields` naming a dedicated parameter no longer fails with `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'parent'`
- `assignee` and `parent` can be cleared at all — `null` was unreachable and `""` answered 422
- An empty reference object (`type={}`) is refused locally with a readable message instead of an unhelpful 400/422
- API errors carry Tracker's own `errorMessages` / `errors` instead of a bare "Unprocessable Entity"
- A 409 on update raises `IssueVersionConflict`, which explains that queue triggers bump the version right after creation, so the version from `issue_create` must not be reused
- A missing queue raises `QueueNotFound` on every queue-scoped read (`queue_get_tags`, `queue_get_versions`, `queue_get_fields`, `queue_get_metadata`), not just the newest ones
- `queue_get_metadata` returns what `expand` asked for, and answers a requested but empty section with an empty list instead of omitting it
- `IssueComment` is a complete model again: `MaillistReference` was declared after the forward reference that used it, leaving the model unbuilt
- `queue_get_fields` and `get_priorities` are described as what they are, so tool search finds them and callers know `get_global_fields` holds the rest

### Internal

- Entity tool and parameter descriptions state shared rules once in the server instructions instead of repeating them per tool, cutting ~21 KB from the manifest

'''
p.write_text(s[:start] + new + s[end:])
print("rewritten")

Переписал. Секция была 71 строка, стала 50.

## Вы были правы — там был мусор от промежуточных коммитов

Записи описывали правки того, что **само появляется в этом же релизе**. Проверил по составу тулов на теге `0.7.3` (39 тулов) против текущего (82, добавлено 43, удалено 0):

| запись | почему выкинул |
|---|---|
| «Drop `with_board` from `goal_delete`» | `goal_delete` новый — параметр никогда не выходил |
| «Paginate entity comments through `/comments/_relative`… instead of returning only the first page» | entity-комментарии новые, «раньше» не было |
| «Fall back to the default field set when `fields` is empty» | то же |
| «`lastCommentUpdatedAt` typed as `datetime`» | поле есть только в новых entity-моделях |
| «Issue templates expose a single, normalized `description`» | шаблоны новые — свернул в описание фичи |
| «Reject an entity update that would only change `links`» | свернул в фичу как поведение, а не как фикс |
| «Describe `*_update_checklist` as the bulk edit that it is» | то же |

## Что ещё исправил по пути

Нашёл фактическую ошибку в записи про `QueueNotFound`: перечислялись имена методов протокола и несуществующий тул `queue_get`. Реальные тулы — `queue_get_tags`, `queue_get_versions`, `queue_get_fields`, `queue_get_metadata`.

И пересчитал тулы, потому что чуть не записал 43 entity-тула: 43 — это всё добавленное с 0.7.3, из них 4 — шаблоны. Entity-тулов 39, манифест растёт с 43 до 82. Сверил запуском сервера.

## Полнота

Прошёлся по всем 16 коммитам с 0.7.3 — каждый представлен. Проверил, что всё заявленное существует в коде: `TRACKER_API_TIMEOUT`, `TRACKER_ENTITIES_ENABLED`, `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES` подтвердил через `Settings.model_fields` (грепом их не видно — pydantic выводит имена из полей), а каждый упомянутый тул — по списку зарегистрированных.

Добавил одну недостающую строку в Internal — про сокращение описаний entity-тулов (−21 KB манифеста), её не было вовсе.

Оставил как есть только то, что действительно меняется относительно 0.7.3: у `issue_create`/`issue_update`, `issues_find`, `issues_count`, `issue_get_comments`, `queue_get_metadata`, `get_priorities` — эти тулы на теге уже были.
